Alum is known to be a neutral felt, confiling of the vitriolic acid and a calcareous earth. When this falt is calcined with the fecal matter, or other fulblances a bounding in oil, the volatile principles of thefe fulblances, fuch as their phlegn, their fats, and their oils, exhale in the fame manner as if they were difficilled; and there is nothing left in the matras; when thofe principles are dilipated, but a charred matter, like that which is found in retorts wherein fuch mixts have been decompoiled by diftillation.

This remainder therefore is nothing but a mixture of alum and charcoal. Now, as the acid of this falt, which is the vitriolic, hath a greater affinity with the phlogilton than with any other fulblance, it will quit its balls to unit with the phlogilton of the coal, and be converted by that union into a fulphur. And this is the very cafe, of which we have certain proofs in the operation for pre- paling this phofphorus; for when, after the volatile principles of the oily matter are drawn off, the fire is increased, in order to combine closely together the fixed parts that remain in the matras, that is, the alum and the charred matter, we perceive at the mouth of the ma- tras a final blue fulphureous flame, and a pungent fmell of burning fulphur.
